extra_vocab.en: to try very hard to do or get something
extra_vocab.note: 在這篇演講裡，constantly strive to achieve more 描述人們不斷拚命想得到更多成就，帶有「很辛苦、停不下來」的語感。商務文件常用 strive to / strive for 表達公司或團隊的目標與態度。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: strive 是不規則動詞（strive–strove–striven），也可寫 strived；後面接 to + 原形動詞，或用 strive for + 名詞，不直接接受詞。

example.en: Our company strives to deliver every order on time.
example.zh: 我們公司努力讓每筆訂單準時送達。

example.en: The sales team strove to reach its target before the end of March.
example.zh: 業務團隊努力在三月底前達成目標。

example.en: We have striven to keep our prices low despite higher costs.
example.zh: 儘管成本變高，我們仍努力維持低價。

example.en: Striving for perfect results can sometimes delay the whole project.
example.zh: 一味追求完美的結果，有時會拖延整個專案。

example.en: We strive for excellence in every customer interaction.
example.zh: 我們在每一次與顧客的互動中都追求卓越。

example.en: All employees should strive to improve their skills.
example.zh: 所有員工都應該努力提升自己的技能。

example.en: We always strive for better results than last quarter.
example.zh: 我們總是力求比上一季有更好的成果。

examples.en: We should strive to finish the project before the end of June.
examples.zh: 我們應該努力在六月底前完成這個專案。

examples.en: The brand strives to make every customer feel welcome.
examples.zh: 這個品牌努力讓每位顧客都感到受歡迎。

examples.en: Employees are encouraged to strive for higher goals each year.
examples.zh: 公司鼓勵員工每年追求更高的目標。

confusable.diff: thrive /θraɪv/ 是「興旺、茁壯」，指發展得很好；strive 是「努力」，指付出行動。

example.en: Small businesses thrive when customers feel welcome.
example.zh: 當顧客感到受歡迎時，小型企業就會興旺。

confusable.diff: strike /straɪk/ 是「罷工、打擊」，開頭與母音都和 strive 很像，但意思不同。

example.en: The workers voted to strike if the company cut their pay.
example.zh: 工人投票決定，如果公司減薪就要罷工。

confusable.diff: struggle 常翻成「奮鬥」，但意思是在困難中掙扎；strive 強調有目標、積極地努力。

example.en: Many small firms struggle to pay rent during the winter.
example.zh: 許多小公司在冬天難以支付租金。

similar.diff: endeavor 較正式、書面，常用在公司聲明中；strive 比較常見，語氣也更有力。

example.en: We endeavor to respond to all e-mails within one business day.
example.zh: 我們盡力在一個工作天內回覆所有郵件。

similar.diff: try to 最口語、最日常，只說「嘗試」；strive to 表示持續、用力地努力。

example.en: Please try to arrive ten minutes before the meeting starts.
example.zh: 請盡量在會議開始前十分鐘到場。

example.en: The team made a great effort to finish on time.
example.zh: 團隊很努力地想準時完成。

example.en: Our main goal this year is to open three new stores.
example.zh: 我們今年的主要目標是開三家新店。

example.en: Her ambition is to lead the sales department one day.
example.zh: 她的抱負是有一天領導業務部門。

extra_vocab.en: to finish something or reach a goal successfully
extra_vocab.note: 在這篇演講裡，what we accomplish 指我們「完成了什麼」，講者提醒不要只用成就來衡量人生價值。商務情境常用來談目標、任務與成果，語氣比 do 或 finish 更正式。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: accomplish 是及物動詞，直接接受詞：accomplish a goal；不能說 accomplish to do something。

example.en: The new software accomplishes in minutes what used to take hours.
example.zh: 這套新軟體幾分鐘就能完成過去要花好幾個小時的工作。

example.en: The team accomplished all of its goals before the deadline.
example.zh: 團隊在截止日前達成了所有目標。

example.en: She is an accomplished manager with fifteen years of experience.
example.zh: 她是一位有十五年經驗、很有成就的經理。

example.en: Accomplishing this task will require help from three departments.
example.zh: 要完成這項任務，需要三個部門的協助。

example.en: It took two years to accomplish a goal that seemed impossible.
example.zh: 花了兩年才達成這個看似不可能的目標。

example.en: The software helps staff accomplish a task in half the time.
example.zh: 這套軟體讓員工用一半的時間就能完成一項工作。

example.en: I hope to accomplish a lot during my first week.
example.zh: 我希望在第一週就完成很多事。

examples.en: What did you accomplish during your first month at the company?
examples.zh: 你進公司第一個月完成了什麼？

examples.en: Together, we can accomplish much more than any single department.
examples.zh: 合作起來，我們能完成的遠比任何單一部門多。

examples.en: The manager praised the team for what they had accomplished.
examples.zh: 經理稱讚團隊所完成的成果。

confusable.diff: accompany /əˈkʌmpəni/ 是「陪同、伴隨」，拼法與開頭音節都像 accomplish，但意思不同。

example.en: A guide will accompany the visitors during the factory tour.
example.zh: 參觀工廠時，會有一位導覽人員陪同訪客。

confusable.diff: achieve 強調達到較高的目標或成就；accomplish 強調把任務或工作完成，常用於具體的事。

example.en: The company hopes to achieve record sales this year.
example.zh: 公司希望今年達到創紀錄的銷售額。

similar.diff: complete 只是「做完」，語氣中性；accomplish 還帶有「成功完成」的成就感。

example.en: Please complete the form and return it by Friday.
example.zh: 請填完表格，並在星期五前交回。

example.en: We set a clear goal for each quarter.
example.zh: 我們為每一季訂下明確的目標。

example.en: The main objective of the meeting is to approve the budget.
example.zh: 這場會議的主要目的是核准預算。

derived.link: accomplish + -ment，把「完成」變成名詞，像 payment、agreement

extra_vocab.en: to fail to notice something, or to look down on a place from above
extra_vocab.note: 在這篇演講裡，something we often overlook 指「我們常忽略的事」，也就是時間是有限的這件事。商務情境中最常用在審查、報告與品管，表示沒注意到細節或錯誤；另一個常見意思是房間、建築「俯瞰」某處。

example.en: The manager rarely overlooks small errors in the monthly report.
example.zh: 經理很少漏看月報告裡的小錯誤。

example.en: The auditor overlooked one invoice, so the total was wrong.
example.zh: 稽核員漏看了一張發票，所以總額是錯的。

example.en: Overlooking small details can lead to expensive mistakes.
example.zh: 忽略小細節可能導致昂貴的錯誤。

example.en: Please do not overlook a detail when you check the contract.
example.zh: 檢查合約時，請不要漏看任何細節。

example.en: Some safety rules are easily overlooked by new staff.
example.zh: 有些安全規定很容易被新進員工忽略。

example.en: The new office will overlook the harbor and the main square.
example.zh: 新辦公室將俯瞰港口與主廣場。

examples.en: We cannot overlook this problem any longer.
examples.zh: 我們不能再忽視這個問題了。

examples.en: It is easy to overlook the cost of maintenance.
examples.zh: 維修成本很容易被忽略。

examples.en: Please check again so that we do not overlook any errors.
examples.zh: 請再檢查一次，以免漏掉任何錯誤。

confusable.diff: oversee /ˌoʊvərˈsiː/ 是「監督、管理」，開頭 over- 與重音位置都和 overlook 很像，但意思不同。

example.en: She will oversee the new product launch next month.
example.zh: 她將負責監督下個月的新產品上市。

confusable.diff: ignore 是明知道卻不理會；overlook 多半是沒有注意到，兩者中文都常翻成「忽略」。

example.en: The supplier ignored our warning and shipped the wrong parts.
example.zh: 供應商無視我們的警告，還是寄出了錯誤的零件。

confusable.diff: look over 是「仔細查看、檢查」，字根都有 look，但意思幾乎相反。

example.en: Could you look over the contract before I send it?
example.zh: 我寄出之前，你可以先看一下這份合約嗎？

example.en: Some firms neglect staff training during busy seasons.
example.zh: 有些公司在旺季時會忽略員工訓練。

example.en: Did you notice the mistake on page two?
example.zh: 你有注意到第二頁的錯誤嗎？

example.en: I almost missed the deadline for the application.
example.zh: 我差點錯過申請的截止日期。

senses.en: to fail to notice or think about something

example.en: Many managers overlook the importance of regular feedback.
example.zh: 許多主管忽略了定期給予回饋的重要性。

senses.en: to have a view of a place from above
senses.distinguish: 主詞是房間、建築或窗戶，後面接海、公園、城市時，指俯瞰。

example.en: From the meeting room, you can overlook the whole city.
example.zh: 從會議室可以俯瞰整座城市。

senses.en: to choose not to punish or complain about a mistake
senses.distinguish: 後面接某人的過失，且前面有 agree to、choose to 時，指這次睜一隻眼閉一隻眼。

example.en: The supervisor agreed to overlook the late report this time.
example.zh: 主管同意這次不追究遲交的報告。

extra_vocab.en: to understand how good or important something is and enjoy it
extra_vocab.note: 在這篇演講裡，to appreciate the world around us 是「用心欣賞、珍惜周遭的世界」，並不是單純說謝謝。結尾的 appreciate where we are right now 也是這個意思；商務書信中更常見的是「感激」。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: appreciate 後面直接接名詞或 V-ing，不接 to + 原形；請求對方時用 I would appreciate it if you could ...，中間的 it 不能省略。

example.en: The director always appreciates a clear and short report.
example.zh: 主任總是欣賞清楚又簡短的報告。

example.en: Your quick reply was greatly appreciated by the whole team.
example.zh: 您迅速的回覆讓整個團隊深表感激。

example.en: Appreciating employees' efforts helps keep morale high.
example.zh: 肯定員工的努力有助於維持士氣。

example.en: I really appreciate your help with the budget report.
example.zh: 我真的很感謝你協助處理預算報告。

example.en: We appreciate the opportunity to work with your company.
example.zh: 我們很感謝有機會與貴公司合作。

example.en: Any feedback on the draft would be greatly appreciated.
example.zh: 對於草稿的任何意見，我們都非常感激。

example.en: I would appreciate it if you could reply by Friday.
example.zh: 如果您能在星期五前回覆，我會很感激。

examples.en: Thank you; we appreciate your patience during the repair work.
examples.zh: 謝謝您；我們感謝您在維修期間的耐心。

examples.en: Customers appreciate honest advice more than a strong sales pitch.
examples.zh: 比起強力推銷，顧客更欣賞誠實的建議。

examples.en: Visitors appreciate the quiet atmosphere of the old town.
examples.zh: 遊客很欣賞老城區安靜的氣氛。

confusable.diff: appraise /əˈpreɪz/ 是「評價、估價」，開頭拼法與發音都像 appreciate，但不表示感激。

example.en: An expert will appraise the building before we buy it.
example.zh: 購買之前，專家會先為這棟建築估價。

confusable.diff: depreciate /dɪˈpriːʃieɪt/ 是「貶值」，字根相同、後半音節完全一樣，但意思與 appreciate 的「增值」相反。

example.en: Company cars usually depreciate quickly in the first year.
example.zh: 公司的車子在第一年通常貶值得很快。

similar.diff: thank 後面接人（thank you），appreciate 後面接事物（appreciate your help）。

example.en: We would like to thank everyone who joined the event.
example.zh: 我們想感謝所有參加活動的人。

similar.diff: value 作動詞是「重視」，語氣較強調重要性；appreciate 更強調欣賞與感受到好處。

example.en: We value your opinion and read every survey carefully.
example.zh: 我們重視您的意見，也會仔細閱讀每份問卷。

example.en: We are grateful for your support this year.
example.zh: 我們感謝您今年的支持。

example.en: She expressed her gratitude to the whole team.
example.zh: 她向整個團隊表達感謝。

example.en: The company will recognize outstanding employees at the annual dinner.
example.zh: 公司將在年終晚宴上表揚傑出員工。

derived.link: appreciate 去掉 e + -ion，動詞變名詞，像 create → creation

senses.en: to understand the value of something and enjoy it

example.en: It takes time to appreciate the quality of this craftsmanship.
example.zh: 要花時間才能欣賞這件工藝品的品質。

senses.en: to feel thankful for something someone did
senses.distinguish: 後面接 your help、your support、your reply 等別人做的事時，指感謝。

example.en: We appreciate your quick response to our request.
example.zh: 我們感謝您迅速回應我們的要求。

senses.en: to become more valuable over time
senses.distinguish: 主詞是房產、股票、貨幣等資產時，指價值上升，是不及物動詞。

example.en: Property in this area is expected to appreciate over the next decade.
example.zh: 預期這個地區的房地產在未來十年會增值。

senses.en: to understand a situation or a problem
senses.distinguish: 後面接 that 子句或 the difficulty 等狀況時，指理解對方的處境。

example.en: I appreciate that the deadline is tight, but accuracy matters.
example.zh: 我理解截止日期很緊，但準確性很重要。

extra_vocab.en: to use something as well as you can
extra_vocab.note: 在這篇演講的結尾，let's make the most of the time we have 是呼籲大家好好把握手上的時間。後面常接時間、機會、資源或預算，語氣正面、積極。
extra_vocab.pattern: make the most of + N（時間／機會／資源）
extra_vocab.grammar_note: 固定說法要寫成 make the most of，中間的 the 不能省略；of 後面接名詞或代名詞（it、this），不接原形動詞。

examples.en: Let's make the most of this meeting and finish the agenda early.
examples.zh: 讓我們善用這場會議，提早完成議程。

examples.en: She made the most of her business trip by visiting two clients.
examples.zh: 她善用這趟出差，順道拜訪了兩位客戶。

examples.en: Employees should make the most of the training sessions this month.
examples.zh: 員工應該好好把握本月的訓練課程。

examples.en: We must make the most of our limited budget this year.
examples.zh: 我們今年必須善用有限的預算。

similar.diff: take advantage of 是「利用」機會或優惠，有時也帶有占別人便宜的負面意思；make the most of 是把握到最好。

example.en: We should take advantage of the early booking discount.
example.zh: 我們應該把握提早訂位的優惠。

similar.diff: make good use of 強調「好好運用」手上的東西，語氣比較平實，沒有「發揮到極致」的感覺。

example.en: The team made good use of the new software.
example.zh: 團隊善用了這套新軟體。

confusable.diff: make the best of 是在情況不理想時「盡量往好處做」；make the most of 是把好的機會或資源發揮到最大。

example.en: We cannot change the schedule, so let's make the best of it.
example.zh: 我們無法更改時程，所以讓我們盡量把事情做好。

confusable.diff: most of the 是「大部分的」，拼法相近，但不是動詞片語，只用來表示數量。

example.en: Most of the staff arrived before nine o'clock.
example.zh: 大部分的員工在九點前就到了。
